//: Proves the permission-free path end to end: capture the page over the DevTools protocol, write the events sidecar from the actions performed, encode the frames into a raw take, and style it through the same renderer the screen recorder's output goes through. No DemoTape app running, no Screen Recording grant, no Accessibility grant, no network, no account.
//why: This is the one-command story. The native path needs the app installed and running with two permissions granted before anyone sees a video; that setup is most of the reason a first run takes ten minutes instead of one line. Here the browser is headless, the pointer is recorded rather than moved, and the renderer draws it afterwards from the samples.
//check: Afterwards, in the temp capture folder: manifest.json lists the frames, capture.events.json must have a non-empty `clicks` array and `keys` with INCREASING x (the caret being followed), and capture.styled.mp4 should show the auto-zoom firing on the click. `--frame` a still around the click to look at it.
//limits: Only the page viewport is captured — no browser chrome, no desktop, no webcam — and JPEG costs some fidelity. Use the native path for a demo of the whole screen.
